CCHRC hosted the subcontract with NREL and, critically, provided necessary financial match. 2 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. 3.0 Project Objectives Originally, the project aimed to achieve annual energy cost reductions based on initial audit recommendations of 13% to 18% across four buildings: Tribal Office, Community Center, Duplex, AVCP Office). However, financial limitations and COVID-19 disruptions compelled NVA to focus exclusively on the Tribal Office (Figure 1), targeting a 16% reduction in energy costs through high-impact retrofits, i.e., retrofits that could result in a quick return on investment without exceeding the available budget. This strategic pivot sought to maximize economic benefits and provide a framework for future community- wide energy improvements. Figure 1: Aniak Tribal Office. Photo credit J. Fowler/Energy Audits of Alaska. 3 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. 4.0 Description of Activities Performed To achieve these objectives, NREL, NVA, and an energy auditor completed the following tasks between November 2022 and May 2025. Overview Task 1: Project Kickoff In the first quarter of the project, NVA staff, NREL staff, and the energy auditor met virtually to review project goals and finalize planning documents. The Tribal Office was benchmarked against a 2017 energy audit. The building’s annual energy usage was assessed in terms of energy use intensity (EUI) and fuel oil usage relative to cumulative base 65o heating degree days (HDDs) across the sample period to understand each building’s performance over time further and investigate potential energy anomalies. This project—originally intended to implement energy efficiency retrofits for four Aniak buildings audited in 2017—faced significant delays because of the COVID-19 pandemic and workforce capacity issues. 1.1 Document the present conditions of the project buildings: The energy auditor (re)documented the current conditions in the four buildings and noted some changes since the earlier energy audit. 1.2 Create a data management plan: Staff developed a data management plan detailing roles and responsibilities for the energy savings verification process. The plan outlined methods for data collection and secure storage throughout the project duration. 1.3 Create an outreach plan: Staff developed an outreach plan to inform and educate Tribal members about the project scope and the benefits of energy efficiency upgrades. 1.4 COVID mitigation plan: At the time of implementation, NVA no longer required this subtask. Task 2: Hire Retrofit Contractors Project staff developed detailed scopes of work for lighting and mechanical systems. Requests for Proposals (RFPs) were issued, and at least three bids were obtained for each category. Contractors were hired by the end of the third quarter of the project. After re-evaluating the scope of work in 2023, the focus was narrowed to the Tribal Office.
